'''Svetlana Alekseevna Gannushkina''' ({{langx|ru|Светла́на Алексе́евна Га́ннушкина}}, born 6 March 1942) is a mathematician and [[human rights]] activist in [[Russia]] who was reported to have been a serious contender for the 2010 [[Nobel Peace Prize]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/technology/8560469.stm |title= Internet 'in running' for Nobel Peace Prize |author= |date=10 March 2010 |website= |publisher=[[BBC News]] |accessdate=19 January 2012}}</ref> 

Gannushkina became well-known in Russia as a human rights defender in 1990s when many conflicts broke in the countries of the former Soviet Union. Her human rights work dedicated especially to help refugees, [[internally displaced person]]s, victims of war.<ref name="democracy">{{cite web |url=https://www.opendemocracy.net/en/odr/interview-svetlana-gannushkina/ |title="We don't need the State Department to hold a revolution" |last=Liubakova  |first=Hanna |date=December 20, 2018 |website=opendemocracy.net |access-date=July 21, 2021 }}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Gannushkina was born in Moscow on March 6, 1942. 
She graduated from the [[MSU Faculty of Mechanics and Mathematics| Moscow State University's Faculty of Mechanics and Mathematics]].<ref name="president-bio">{{cite web |url=http://president-sovet.ru/projects/bibliography/read/122/ |title=Светлана Ганнушкина: «У меня, что называется, дурная привычка лезть в чужие дела» |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=October 31, 2018 |website=president-sovet.ru |access-date=July 23, 2021 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200721001005/http://president-sovet.ru/projects/bibliography/read/122/ |archive-date=July 21, 2020}}</ref>

==Work==
Gannushkina worked for many years as a professor of mathematics at the [[Russian State University for the Humanities]].<ref name="president-bio" /> In 1990, she helped to found the [[Civic Assistance Committee]] (Komitet Grazhdanskoe Sodeistvie), an NGO which campaigns for human rights, particularly with regard to immigrants and refugees in Russian society.<ref name="bbcG61016"/> Since 2015, the organization is labelled a "[[Russian foreign agent law|foreign agent]]" by the [[Russian government]].<ref name="bbcG61016">[https://www.bbc.com/news/world-37558076 The Nobel Peace Prize: Who will win this year?], [[BBC News]] (6 October 2016)</ref>

Gannushkina was a member of [[Presidential Council for Civil Society and Human Rights]] until 2011.<ref name="president-bio" /><ref name=AI>{{cite web |url=https://www.amnesty.org/en/news-and-updates/feature-stories/human-rights-defender-russia-svetlana-alekseevna-gannushkina-20081209 |title=Human Rights Defender in Russia: Svetlana Alekseevna Gannushkina |author= |date=9 December 2008 |website= |publisher=[[Amnesty International]] |accessdate=19 January 2012}}</ref> She is also on the council of [[Memorial (society)|Memorial]], a society dedicated to the remembrance of victims of Soviet repression.

Gannushkina is a member of the [[Yabloko]] Federal Political Committee.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Федеральный политический комитет|url=https://www.yabloko.ru/content/politicheskii_komitet|access-date=2021-07-23|website=Партия Яблоко|language=ru}}</ref>

==Awards==

* 1997 [[Open Society Foundations]] prize for trailblazing work in Russia.<ref name="president-bio" />  

* 2006 [[Homo Homini Award]] for human rights activism by the Czech group [[People in Need (Czech Republic)|People in Need]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.clovekvtisni.cz/index2en.php?id=549|title=Previous Recipients of the Homo Homini Award|author=|date=|website=|publisher=[[People In Need (Czech Republic)|People in Need]]|access-date=17 April 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110501192644/http://www.clovekvtisni.cz/index2en.php?id=549|archive-date=1 May 2011}}</ref>

* 2016 [[Right Livelihood Award]], often referred to as "Alternative Nobel Prize", in [[Stockholm]], Sweden, "''for her decades-long commitment to promoting human rights and justice for refugees and forced migrants, and tolerance among different ethnic groups''".<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.rightlivelihoodaward.org/laureates/svetlana-gannushkina/|title=Svetlana Gannushkina {{!}} The Right Livelihood Award|website=www.rightlivelihoodaward.org|language=en-US|access-date=14 May 2018}}</ref>
